articles.title: James Gunn and Peter Safran’s DC Experiment: What’s Working, What Isn’t, and What’s Next
articles.summary: Four years and three movies into a total rebuild, we review — and grade — the latest iteration of the DC Universe.
articles.content: Four years ago this week , James Gunn and Peter Safran were handed one of Hollywood’s most coveted, and impossible, jobs. When they were named co-CEOs of Warner Bros.’ DC Studios label, they received complete oversight of comic book characters like Superman, Wonder Woman, Batman* (more on that later), Green Lantern, the Flash, and countless others. With a seemingly blank canvas to make as many movies and shows as their hearts desired, the implied mandate was clear: get DC Comics out of second place. The studio’s DC division spent much of the 2010s as a laughingstock while its Marvel competitors seemed to never miss. Despite having a better roster of characters — 20 years ago, mentioning the Guardians of the Galaxy in the same breath as Batman would have been laughable even to the biggest comic book nerd — Warner Bros. couldn’t figure out how to turn its characters into must-see cinema. The incredible cultural moment of the Christopher Nolan Batman movies gave way to one misfire after another: Zack Snyder’s “Man of Steel” gave way to the “Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice” debacle, Patty Jenkins’ acclaimed “Wonder Woman” movie led to a critically panned sequel, and the studio’s attempt to launch its own “Avengers” with “Justice League” was bad enough to leave fans arguing about different cuts instead of wondering where the story went next. articles.title: From ‘The Devils’ to ‘Obsession,’ How ‘Femcel’ Horror Handles Horny Women
articles.summary: With Ken Russell's "The Devils" thriving in theaters, horror is still obsessed with the dangers of female desire. Offscreen, real women are questioning if romance is worth wanting at all.
articles.content: Has sexual violence always been a spectator sport? It certainly has an audience. Last week, prediction market Polymarket removed a contract that allowed users to bet on whether any of the seven men accused of sexually assaulting a Cornell University student in an alleged gang rape would face felony sex-crime charges. The men have broadly denied the allegations, and no one has been criminally charged. But before the Polymarket contract came down, bets about the Cornell case generated more than $450,000 in trading volume — suggesting that just the prospect of accountability for claims of alleged sexual violence can be repackaged and sold as dark entertainment today. Related Stories Walter Koenig, Actor Who Played Chekov on ‘Star Trek,’ Dies at 90 How ‘The Only Living Pickpocket in New York’ Used Vintage ‘Godfather’ Lenses to Capture NYC on Location Ken Russell ’s “ The Devils ” understood the power of that spectacle 55 years ago. Now enjoying an extended theatrical run following its long-awaited restoration, the notorious 1971 film reveals how readily powerful institutions can turn women’s private experiences into public theater. In Russell’s feverish account of religious repression, a nun’s unrequited lust for a priest becomes a political weapon: a message that’s only grown more resonant in an era of increasing cruelty online. In the decades since, horror hasn’t stopped asking what happens when women want too much. If anything, the cultural fascination with female rage has made those questions more urgent and their resolutions more complicated. Starting Monday, Instagram will be launching a test of horizontal videos of up to 90 minutes with select creators in the U.S. The product, called Features, is aimed at podcasters, comedians and other longform creators, with the ability to refer viewers to the full video from the shortform reels on the platform, which are typically around three minutes or less. “What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” said Tessa Lyons, vp product at Instagram. Here is an excerpt from Vadim Rizov’s IndieWire review : “By revisiting his debut feature, 2001’s ‘La libertad,’ Lisandro Alonso accomplished several goals. By re-staging entire sequences from his minimally-minded breakout of trees being chopped and sanded down, Alonso accentuates the passage of time in the simplest possible way: watching the same visibly changed logger (Misael Saavedra) perform the same tasks 25 years later with no further comment. By introducing broader social context, including the logger’s sister set adrift by a collapsing medical/social safety net, Alonso makes the point that the world has worsened, expanding a laconic portrait of a singular time and place to include previously ignorable grim realities. Finally, in revisi(ti)ng a film whose ending he was forced to change at the behest of Cannes Film Festival head Thierry Frémaux in order to get in, Alonso gets to restore his original ending — a great example of long-stocked petty resentments turned productive.”

articles.title: Hubert de la Bouillerie Dies: Editor On ‘Woodstock’, ‘Witches Of Eastwick’, ‘Rollerball’ & Others Was 75
articles.content: Hubert de la Bouillerie , a film editor whose credits range from the influential documentary Woodstock , And Justice for All and Rollerball to The Witches of Eastwick, two Police Academy movies, Tango and Cash and Celtic Pride , has died. He was 75. De la Bouillerie died August 8 in Los Angeles, but his death is just being reported by his family. His sister Annie Goeke-de la Bouillerie said he had battled a long-term illness and was in hospice the last two weeks of his life. De la Bouillerie began his career on a high note as an editor on the Oscar-winning documentary Woodstock, which chronicled the landmark 1969 music festival that defined the counterculture generation. Thelma Schoonmaker earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Film Editing. He went on to work as an assistant editor on such 1970s and early-’80s films as Rollerball , And Justice for All and Firefox along with TV’s Roots: The Next Generations and Supertrain before landing his first editor credit with the 1985 jailhouse comedy Doin’ Time. From there, de la Bouillerie editor such features as Highlander II: The Quickening , For Better or Worse, Other People’s Morey, Mo’ Money , Blank Check , Celtic Pride and the fifth and sixth installments of comedy franchise Police Academy. He also directed some films in the mid-1990s, telepics including The Right to Remain Silent and The Apocalypse and a 2005 episode of David E. Kelley’s ABC legal drama Boston Legal. In all, he cut more than 30 movies and TV programs during a three-decade career. Born on January 28, 1951, in France, de la Bouillerie was educated in that country and served in its military. Most of his adult and professional life was spent in the U.S., particularly in Los Angeles. He also was an accomplished photographer and writer. His debut novel Of Love and Evil: The Birth was published in 2012. De la Bouillerie is survived by his children Jacqueline Bell and Alexandre de la Bouillerie and siblings Annie Goeke, Caroline Gruber, Juliette Glazebro

articles.title: Walter Koenig Dies: ‘Star Trek’s Original Ensign Chekov Was 90
articles.content: Walter Koenig , who originated the role of Ensign Pavel Chekov in the 1960s Star Trek TV series and several subsequent movies about the adventures of the USS Enterprise, died Sunday, according to his rep. He was 90. Zachery McGinnis of Galactic Productions posted Monday on Facebook that Koenig died of natural causes in North Hollywood but did not provide other details. “Walter’s legacy extends far beyond the screen,” McGinnis wrote in part. “Through countless convention appearances and interactions with fans, he shared his kindness, wit, and appreciation with everyone fortunate enough to meet him. He understood what Star Trek meant to people and embraced the community that grew around it.” George Takei, who played Sulu on the original Star Trek , also posted on Koenig’s death. See his and McGinnis’ posts below. Koenig played the Russian navigator Chekov in second and third seasons of NBC’s Star Trek series from 1967-69 and reprised the role in the first seven Star Trek films from 1979-94. The character’s introduction for Season 2 came at the height of the U.S.-USSR Cold War. The news comes as the original hugely popular, influential and low-budget Star Trek series created by Gene Roddenberry is marking its 60th anniversary . The show also was notable for its iconoclastic diversity for a mid-century TV series. Born on September 14, 1936, in Chicago, Koenig had a brief early career as a dancer before turning to acting. His earliest roles including guest spots on such 1960s TV series as Combat!, The Untouchables, Ben Casey, Gidget, I Spy, The Alfred Hitchcock Hour and Jericho. He also appeared in the 1963 pilot episode of what would become one of TV’s most popular soap operas, ABC’s General Hospital. But his big break would come with Star Trek in 1967 — the start of a 25-year journey as navigator of the starship USS Enterprise. The original series launched a universe that has kept tens of millions of Earthlings, known as Trekkies or Trekkers, enthralled for six decades

articles.content: Julian Fellowes attended The Gilded Age ‘s Season 4 premiere at the Plaza Hotel in New York City, where he thanked Casey Bloys for believing in the series from the start. “I have a special place in my heart for Casey Bloys, our protector, our gladiator, our defender from very, very early days,” Fellowes said before the screening. “Anyone who enjoys the show owes him a great deal. I certainly do, and I say that with both pride and happiness.” Deadline reported in 2019 that, after NBC ordered the series, the creator’s vision for the period piece proved too ambitious for the constraints of broadcast TV. Universal TV shopped the series, and it landed at HBO in a competitive situation. The series finally premiered in 2022, with Season 4 debuting on Sunday, November 1. During the presentation, Fellowes also gave a shout-out to NBCU’s Pearlena Igbokwe as “one of the first to recognize” the specialness of the series. He also mentioned Bob Greenblatt for not letting it rest and for making the series, and called HBO’s Francesca Orsi “wonderful” for bringing the series home. Watch on Deadline Fellowes said that he had always been interested in the Gilded Age, calling it “a very interesting period of American history,” adding, “I think it was the beginning of modern America, and it was the moment that America decided they didn’t want to copy Europe and have five generations before anyone could be invited for dinner and all that kind of thing.” “Whatever one says about the so-called robber barons, the fact is, within a few years, the century would begin what we would know of as the American century,” he continued. “And in both world wars, the voice of America was the loudest at the peace table, because America had arrived, and it was the big, giant new power of the world.”

articles.content: “ Gondhal ,” the Marathi-language thriller India has put forward for the international feature Oscar at the 99th Academy Awards, has launched its global trailer as its awards push moves into a new phase. The film is the first feature from writer-director Santosh Davakhar. It was chosen from a field of 33 films in contention for India’s submission. The story plays out over a single night in rural Maharashtra, during a Gondhal, a folk ritual in which devotion is expressed through song, dance and theatrical storytelling. Ishita Deshmukh plays Suman, a young wife stuck in a suffocating marriage. She tries to take back control by playing on the fixation her lover Sarjerao (Nishad Bhoir) has developed for her. As her desires run up against codes of honor and custom, the night ends in tragedy. Related Stories Emmys Move to Prime Video in Six-Year, Global Deal Worth Around $15 Million a Year Kishor Kadam, Yogesh Sohoni and Anuj Prabhu also star. Legendary composer Ilaiyaraaja wrote the music and background score. “Global perceptions of Indian cinema are often shaped by narratives of poverty and caste conflict – important realities, but not the complete expression of India,” said Davakhar. “India is also a civilization of extraordinary cultural wealth, sustained by traditions, music, and collective memory. Jury members at the festival called the film “like a Shakespearean fable set in a real world.” Davakhar produced the film with Diksha Davakhar, his co-founder at production banner Davakhar Films. His reps said in a statement, “Today we mourn the passing of Walter Koenig, whose talent, warmth, and unforgettable performances left a lasting mark on generations of fans around the world. He passed of old age at home in North Hollywood last night surrounded by his daughter and niece. articles.title: ‘Mirzapur’ Tops a Decade of Indian Streaming as New Commissions Fall, IMDb Report Finds (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.content: Viewer interest in Indian shows on IMDb rose about 17-fold over the past decade, even as the number of new shows and seasons commissioned in the country has dropped for two straight years, according to a new IMDb study that traces the growth of Indian streaming through its most popular titles. “10 Years of Streaming in India – An IMDb Report 2026” draws on page views from the more than 250 million people who visit IMDb worldwide each month. It ranks each year’s 10 biggest Indian series from 2016 to 2026, a total of 110 slots filled by 64 different shows. It also looks past the top tier at how viewing habits and production patterns have shifted, including the rise of streaming franchises. Crime and thriller titles took 48 of the 110 positions. In the later years, horror, romance, comedy and drama all made gains. Among streamers, Prime Video and Amazon MX Player combined for 34 positions across 17 series, more than any other service. Netflix logged 21 positions spread over 18 series, the broadest range of distinct titles of the platforms the report examined. YouTube emerged as a launchpad. Thirteen of the 64 charting series started life there, and 11 of those were later picked up by subscription services. The report credited the platform with giving a wide base of creators room to build stories that can travel to bigger audiences. The Viral Fever (TVF) stood out on the production side. articles.title: ‘Coven Academy’ Renewed for Season 2 at Disney
articles.content: Disney’s supernatural young adult series “ Coven Academy ” has been renewed for a second season. Created by Tim Federle , the series follows “three teenage witches and their dangerously charming warlock peers at an elite magic boarding school where power is currency, secrets are lethal and attraction is a liability,” per the official logline, which continues: Caught between ancient supernatural wars and forbidden love interests, the coven must decide how far they’re willing to go to protect their city — and themselves.” The cast includes Malina Pauli Weissman, Malachi Barton, Jordan Leftwich, Ora Duplass, Louis Thresher, Tiffani Thiessen and Devon Sawa. articles.title: ‘Baywatch’ Reboot Sets January Premiere Date on Fox
articles.content: “ Baywatch ” is bringing sunshine to the winter, as Fox’s reboot of the blockbuster beach series will premiere on Jan. 6 at 9 p.m. The continuation of the 1990s sensation stars Stephen Amell as a grown-up version of Hobie Buchannon, the wild child from the original series. The show follows Hobie, now a Baywatch Captain, following in the footsteps of his father, Mitch, while his world is turned upside down by the surprise arrival of Charlie (Jessica Belkin), the daughter he never knew. Eager to carry on the family legacy, Charlie strives to become a Baywatch lifeguard alongside her dad. articles.title: Lisa Ling Signs With CAA
articles.content: Lisa Ling , the journalist, producer and author who has logged stints at Channel One, ABC, CNN and CBS News, has tapped CAA to represent her in a variety of fields. Ling, who recently worked as a contributor at CBS News, is known for her work hosting documentary-journalism programs ranging from National Geographic’s “Explorer” to CNN’s “This Is Life.” She also spent time as one of the co-hosts at ABC’s daytime show “The View,” and hosted and executive-produced “Our America” for the Oprah Winfrey Network, now part of Skydance. Related Stories Disney Bids on Character.AI Assets as Chatbot Provider Files for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy 'Dick Clark's New Year's Rockin' Eve With Ryan Seacrest' to Simulcast on Both ABC and Disney+ for the First Time Ling has worked as a journalist from a young age, starting first as a teenager for “Scratch,” a nationally syndicated TV program aimed at teens, and then for Channel One, a video-news report aimed at schoolchildren. She traveled abroad and covered war outbreaks in different parts of the world. She previously had a production deal with HBO that resulted in series such as “Take Out,” a look at the world of Asian-American cuisine. Her books include titles such as “Mother, Sister, Daughter, Bride: Rituals of Womanhood,” and “Somewhere Inside: One Sister’s Captivity in North Korea and Other’s Fights to Bring Her Home,” about her sister, Laura, who was detained in North Korea after attempting to film refugees along the country’s border with China. Ling is founder of MightyLings, a digital platform that promotes intergenerational strength, wellness and spirit building. She serves on the boards of the prison reentry organization CROP, the California Partners Project, The Asian American Foundation and the Kids Mental Health Foundation.

articles.content: “I was my second-choice to direct it,” Aaron Sorkin candidly admitted as we sat down last week at the the Newport Beach Film Festival to record an episode of The Hollywood Reporter ’s Awards Chatter podcast and began discussing the film for which he was receiving the fest’s Maverick Director Award: The Social Reckoning , which he also wrote. This film about Facebook — specifically, about the social media company’s knowledge and cover-up of its harmful effects on society, and the whistleblower (Mikey Madison) who brought them to the attention of a journalist (Jeremy Allen White), creating problems for Mark Zuckerberg (Jeremy Strong) — comes 16 years after another that Sorkin wrote, the massively acclaimed The Social Network , which David Fincher directed. articles.title: Sian Heder Used Her “Moment of Power” After Winning an Oscar to Get ‘Being Heumann’ Made
articles.summary: The 'CODA' filmmaker is back, this time telling the story of disability rights activist Judy Heumann.
articles.content: Four years after CODA took home a best picture Oscar, Sian Heder is back with her follow-up project Being Heumann . Heder — who also landed an Academy Award for adapted screenplay — wrote and directed the film, which tells the story of disability rights activist Judy Heumann. In 1977, Heumann (played by Ruth Madeley) led a 28-day occupation of San Francisco’s Federal Building in a fight for accessibility laws and equal rights. The onscreen retelling, as a result, features a large cast of disabled actors, some of whom are acting for the first time. articles.title: Hubert de la Bouillerie, ‘Woodstock’ and ‘Witches of Eastwick’ Film Editor, Dies at 75
articles.summary: The Warner Bros. veteran also worked on Norman Jewison’s ‘Rollerball’ and ‘Other People’s Money,’ plus ‘Tango & Cash’ and two ‘Police Academy’ movies.
articles.content: Hubert de la Bouillerie, a film editor with credits including Woodstock , Rollerball , The Witches of Eastwick and Tango & Cash , died Aug. 8 in Los Angeles, his friend Robert Folk announced. He was 75. Folk noted that de la Bouillerie was the film editor on the Warner Bros. lot whom longtime studio chiefs Bob Daly and Terry Semel most relied on to review the final edit on “the vast majority of features” that came out of Burbank in the 1980s and ’90s. De la Bouillerie also did some directing; he helmed the 1996 Showtime telefilm The Right to Remain Silent , featuring Lea Thompson and Amanda Plummer; the science-fiction feature The Apocalypse (1997); and a 2005 episode of ABC’s Boston Legal . Related Stories TV Alan Dysert, 'All My Children' Actor, Dies at 75 Movies Tom DeSimone, Director of 'Chatterbox,' 'Hell Night' and 'Reform School Girls,' Dies at 87 He received an additional editing credit on Woodstock (1970) — Martin Scorsese and Thelma Schoonmaker were among the credited film editors on the Michael Wadleigh’s landmark documentary — and served as an assistant editor on Norman Jewison ’s Rollerball (1975). At Warners, he was film editor on George Miller’s The Witches of Eastwick (1987), Police Academy 5: Assignment: Miami Beach (1988), Police Academy 6: City Under Siege (1989), the Sylvester Stallone and Kurt Russell-starring Tango & Cash (1989) and Jewison’s Other People’s Money (1991). Hubert Charles de la Bouillerie was born on Jan. 28, 1951, the eldest child of Baron Henri de la Bouillerie and Elinor Marcus. His paternal family had longstanding ties to the Loire Valley and to the grand Château de Villandry, and he attended the renowned French school École des Roches. In more than three decades of work in Hollywood, his feature editing credits included Krush Groove (1985), Highlander II: The Quickening (1991), Mo’ Money (1992), The Harvest (1993), Blank Check (1994) and Celtic Pride (1996). articles.title: Yes, You Can Still See ‘Musk’ — Here’s What’s Happening With the Film’s Release Plan
articles.summary: The VOD date is being moved up by several weeks even as it continues to play in theaters.
articles.content: Musk , Alex Gibney’s four-hour documentary about the titular mogul and his growing power, is coming to VOD earlier than expected — but hardly being disappeared from the landscape. While some headlines this weekend had suggested the movie was being “pulled,” distributor Bleecker Street is simply preparing to announce a new plan that will give the movie a somewhat shorter runway in theaters and a longer one on VOD. Originally scheduled for a Nov. 24 debut on paid platforms, the movie will now come to paid VOD on Nov. 6. It will continue to play in theaters until then; after playing on 60 screens last weekend, it will be in an as-yet-undetermined number this weekend. Simultaneous plays in theaters after the VOD release are also possible, a company representative said. Bleecker Street also reports that preorders on VOD are strong; indeed, Apple’s top 50 VOD orders for the current week include just two movies that have not been released yet: The Odyssey at No. 10 and Musk at No. 24. Those films land at No. 1 and 2, respectively, on the company’s preorder chart. The film has grossed $650,000 in theaters since its release on Oct. 9, which works out to about 40,000 tickets sold — a number certainly small by many theatrical expectations, but hardly unexpected for a four-hour investigative documentary. A 28-day theatrical window for a documentary before it moves to VOD is also not unusually truncated. The film remains on course to debut on HBO platforms this winter, even as Musk associate David Ellison has now acquired the network. The VOD move-up also extends the amount of time many Americans can see the film should any attempt to censor or stop that release materialize. Gibney’s movie looks at how its subject came to amass so much power and how he has expanded it in the Donald Trump era via DOGE cuts, surveillance, media and broadband takeovers and donations to the Republican Party. articles.title: Tom DeSimone, Director of ‘Chatterbox,’ ‘Hell Night’ and ‘Reform School Girls,’ Dies at 87
articles.summary: He started his career in adult films, where he was “interested in exploring gays in love or at least relationships.”
articles.content: Tom DeSimone, who emerged from the world of 1970s gay adult movies to direct such mainstream cult films as the Linda Blair-starring Hell Night and the women-in-prison flicks The Concrete Jungle and Reform School Girls , has died. He was 87. DeSimone died Oct. 17 in a senior care facility in Palm Springs, his younger brother, actor, comedian and drummer Bob DeSimone ( Friday the 13th: A New Beginning ), told The Hollywood Reporter . He had terminal cancer and opted to end his life with medical assistance. Tom DeSimone also is known for directing the notorious comedy Chatterbox (1977), which starred Candice Rialson as a hairdresser whose vagina talks and has a mind of its (her?) own and featured turns from Rip Taylor and Professor Irwin Corey . articles.content: On October 26, 2001, writer-director Richard Kelly’s Donnie Darko opened in theaters following its Sundance Film Festival bow early in the year. A mixed bag genetically and qualitatively, Darko gyrates around the brooding downward spiral of its titular character, fusing together black comedy, paranormal activity and teenage angst. articles.content: It is a very different look, listen and feel of the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires that Austrian filmmaker Lukas Marxt ( Among the Palms the Bomb, Or: Looking for Reflections in the Toxic Field of Plenty ) brings us in his new experimental documentary. articles.summary: He played Sean Cudahy on the ABC soap for two stretches from 1979 through 1990.
articles.content: Alan Dysert, who portrayed the con man Sean Cudahy on the ABC soap opera All My Children , has died. He was 75. Dysert died Friday, his wife, Michele Dysert, announced on Facebook. He wrote about dealing with a rare, aggressive cancer for more than a dozen years in his 2023 memoir, Lights, Camera, Cancer! “Thank you for loving me, for making me laugh, for the adventures, the memories, and the beautiful life we built together,” she wrote. “I would choose you all over again, without hesitation. My heart is broken, but I am so thankful for the love of a lifetime. I will love you always.” Related Stories Movies Tom DeSimone, Director of 'Chatterbox,' 'Hell Night' and 'Reform School Girls,' Dies at 87 TV Walter Koenig, the Russian Crewman Chekov on 'Star Trek,' Dies at 90 The 6-foot-2 Dysert first showed up as the scheming Sean, brother of the respectable Tom Cudahy (Richard Shoberg), on All My Children in 1979. He left the daytime drama in 1981 but returned for another stint in 1988-90. “My scenes are written better than stuff on nighttime TV,” he told People magazine in a 1981 interview. “This is such a fun role! I love it.” Born on June 12, 1951, Dysert was raised on a farm in Oakwood, Illinois. He graduated from Oakwood High School and the University of Illinois and worked in real estate and did stand-up before landing uncredited roles on a 1978 episode of ABC’s Soap and in Cheech & Chong’s Next Movie (1980). After All My Children , Dysert worked as a producer and director — he wrote, helmed, produced and acted in the 2015 film The Senator — and taught acting in the Nashville area out of The Actor’s School, which he founded in 1991. articles.content: Walter Koenig, the boyish actor who remains an integral part of Star Trek lore thanks to his portrayal of the Russian crewman Pavel Chekov, has died. He was 90. Koenig, also known for playing the scoundrel Alfred Bester on another sci-fi space series, Warner Bros. articles.title: Peggy King, Singer and ‘George Gobel Show’ Star of Television’s Golden Age, Dies at 96
articles.summary: She also recorded several albums for Columbia Records and appeared in Vincente Minnelli’s 'The Bad and the Beautiful.'
articles.content: Peggy King, a television star and singer who rose to prominence in the 1950s, has died. She was 96. King died Sunday after a long battle with Alzheimer’s disease, her publicist Alan Eicher announced. She had been residing at the Saunders House assisted living facility in Wynnewood, Pennsylvania. King was best known for her appearances on The George Gobel Show from 1954-57, where Gobel nicknamed her “Pretty Perky Peggy King.” She won an Emmy in 1955 for best female singer for her television work. She also co-hosted the 1958 Emmys. Related Stories Movies Hubert de la Bouillerie, 'Woodstock' and 'Witches of Eastwick' Film Editor, Dies at 75 TV Alan Dysert, 'All My Children' Actor, Dies at 75 Throughout the 1950s, King appeared on numerous variety programs, including The Bob Hope Show, American Bandstand, The Steve Allen Show, The Jack Benny Program and The Perry Como Show . She also guest-starred on classic television series including Maverick and Dragnet . King signed a contract with MGM in 1952, leading to a singing cameo in Vincente Minnelli’s film The Bad and the Beautiful in which she performed “Don’t Blame Me.” She then appeared in the 1955 horror-comedy Abbott and Costello Meet the Mummy . As for as her music career, King performed “Count Your Blessings (Instead of Sheep)” at the 1955 Academy Awards. After Columbia Records executive Mitch Miller signed her to a long-term contract, she released two best-selling albums, Wish Upon a Star and Girl Meets Boy . DownBeat and Billboard named her best new singer for 1955-56. Composer Arthur Hamilton wrote “Cry Me a River” for King, but Miller refused to let her record it. King later performed the song throughout her career. Born on Feb. 16, 1930, in Greensburg, Pennsylvania, King graduated from Ravenna High School in Ohio. She began singing on the radio in Cleveland before joining bands led by Charlie Spivak, Ray Anthony and Ralph Flanagan. articles.content: Cupertino and Line of Fire are very different shows on screen, but their ratings profiles early in the season are very similar. Both shows draw about 3 million viewers for their initial airings (3.03 million for Cupertino’ s first two episodes on CBS, 2.98 million over three for Line of Fire on NBC). Cupertino and Line of Fire are also picking up a lot of viewing — most of their seven-day totals, in fact — after those initial airings. The 2026-27 TV season is just a month old, so these are necessarily small sample sizes. articles.content: The fund, named after the late television executive and producer, supports arts programs in L.A. public schools The Los Angeles nonprofit organization Young Storytellers has established a fund in honor of late television executive and producer Jamie Tarses . The fund will support the organization’s programs in L.A. public schools, helping volunteer mentors work personally with students to help them write original scripts for professional actors to perform on stage. “Jamie understood that the most powerful thing you can tell a young person is that their ideas deserve to be taken seriously,” Jaylene Benggon Chung, managing director of Young Storytellers, said in a statement. “She built that belief into this organization, and it is still at the center of everything we do. articles.content: The former FBI director’s legal team says that the 2016 article has already been investigated twice and should be dismissed Federal prosecutors again accused James Comey of leaking national security information to the New York Times 10 years ago in a new batch of charges, according to court documents unsealed Monday . The former FBI director’s legal team said that the charges have already been investigated twice but have not led to criminal charges. The recent case involved an Oct. 5, 2016 New York Times article that two different teams of prosecutors investigated during the first Trump administration. articles.title: Watch ‘My Undesirable Friends’ Director Julia Loktev Recall the Week Russia Invaded Ukraine
articles.summary: At IndieWire's Art of the Doc event, Loktev explained why her film about the lives of Russian journalists had to take a different turn.
articles.content: Great documentaries never turn out quite the way you plan them. You might start out thinking that you’re making one film , but a documentarian has to be willing to accept when changes in the lives of their subjects changes the nature of their project. Julia Loktev ‘s two-part documentary “ My Undesirable Friends ” is a perfect example of this. The films, which follow journalists at TV Rain, which was Russia’s last independent news channel before it was shut down over coverage of the war in Ukraine, began as a story about journalists working in a hostile climate. But when her subjects were forced to flee the country and scatter across Europe, “My Undesirable Friends” had to expand its scale. articles.title: ‘Wildwood’ Sparked a Much-Needed Comeback for Laika at the Box Office
articles.summary: Travis Knight's stop-motion animated epic opened to $12.2 million, which is on par with the opening for the company's "Kubo and the Two Strings."
articles.content: The release of Laika ‘s “ Wildwood ” at the box office this weekend was about more than just the dollars and cents or the success or failure of a single film ; in some ways it was about the future of a fan-favorite film studio. “Wildwood” is the Portland, Oregon-based stop-motion animation studio’s sixth animated feature but also the first movie released by the studio in seven years. Easily director Travis Knight’s most ambitious project to date under the Laika banner, it’s been in the works for even longer than that time gap: fans have been awaiting it for years. Heck, we’ve been talking about this movie since last year . What Laika needed with “Wildwood” was not just a solid number but a display of genuine enthusiasm that this movie could reintroduce audiences to the studio. Even if a movie like “ Coraline ,” Laika’s debut, breakout stop-motion hit, was not a gangbusters blockbuster upon its release, it’s a film that has had real staying power and made a legacy for Laika in the process. articles.content: Get the agent, book the studio job, win the award, and so on, collecting infinity stones like Thanos until you can buy that dream house in that quaint part of Studio City. For many working filmmakers, especially women and people of color, the realities of making it in Hollywood are even more nuanced. Recognition can get you into the room, but it does not necessarily get your movie made. Bridget Stokes knows this distinction intimately. When she became the first Black woman to win an Emmy for directing a variety series in 2022 (“A Black Lady Sketch Show”), meetings followed, and congratulations poured in from every angle. She says the award may have earned her more sit-downs when she reached out, but it didn’t produce the career acceleration outsiders might expect. “I didn’t get a [studio] job offer for almost four years after I had won the award,” Stokes said. “Like four years after I had won an Emmy and had this decoration, I never got a job offer.” Related Stories From ‘The Devils’ to ‘Obsession,’ How ‘Femcel’ Horror Handles Horny Women Walter Koenig, Actor Who Played Chekov on ‘Star Trek,’ Dies at 90 Her experience comes amid a contraction that has made an already difficult business considerably harder. articles.title: Walter Koenig, Actor Who Played Chekov on ‘Star Trek,’ Dies at 90
articles.summary: The character actor appeared in seven "Star Trek" films and the original series.
articles.content: Walter Koenig , who played Pavel Andreievich Chekov, a key member of the U.S.S. Enterprise on the original “ Star Trek ” series and across the first seven films, has died. He was 90. As Chekov, a Russian crew member, Koenig spoke in a thick, almost exaggerrated accent and sported a Davy Jones “moptop”. His presence on the bridge was a reminder of Gene Roddenberry’s utopian vision. The original “Star Trek” aired during the height of the Cold War, but it imagined a future in which such regional conflicts had ended in the name of space exploration. Koenig first joined the starship in the show’s second season and would go on to appear in 36 episodes. articles.title: ‘Queen at Sea’ Review: Juliette Binoche Guides Director Lance Hammer Back to Screens with a Searing Film About Dementia and Consent
articles.summary: Binoche and Tom Courtenay star as the fraying family members (and therefore caretakers) of a dementia-addled woman whose time, memory, and function have run out.
articles.content: Lance Hammer was the toast of the town in 2008 with his hard-hitting, Mississippi-set coming-of-age drama “ Ballast .” The Dardennes-esque vérité portrait of lives careening from loss and economic hardship won two awards at the Sundance Film Festival that year — including Best Director for Hammer — and received multiple Film Independent Spirit and Gotham award nominations. He has now returned, almost two decades later, with an extremely upsetting but compassionate moral drama about agency amid dementia, titled “Queen at Sea.” It stars Juliette Binoche as a woman desperate and panicked to take care of her ailing mother, Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall, absolutely shattering in her specificity toward the sickness’ toll), who is slipping deeper into the illness. Leslie’s grasp of time, memory, and function is vanishing in the multi-story London flat she shares with her husband of 19 years, Martin (a brutally heartbreaking Tom Courtenay). Meanwhile, Amanda (Binoche), an academic on sabbatical, is going through a separation herself — from her husband in Newcastle, and now she’s forced to bring her daughter, Sara (Florence Hunt), with her back to London to check in on her mother. articles.title: ‘Clayface’ Tops the Box Office with $24 Million. What Does It Signal About DC Studios’ Latest Reboot?
articles.summary: James Gunn and Peter Safran were brought in to revitalize the comic book brand with mixed results.
articles.content: “ Clayface ,” a body-horror film based on a little-known comic book, opened to $24 million, a middling result for DC Studios, which is in year two of its mixed-bag theatrical revival. On the one hand, the gross isn’t bad considering that the title character is a niche player and the gory genre isn’t associated with the spandex set. On the other, it’s slightly below projections, which predicted that “Clayface” would open to between $25 million to $30 million. It was enough to hold off the second weekend of A24’s “You Can See Everything,” which earned $19.5 million. It also helps that “Clayface” is cheaper than most comic book movies, carrying a price tag of $44 million. It may not be a profit-generating machine, but it won’t lose money either. It also received a critical drubbing. “Clayface” fared better in that respect too. It stands at 75% “fresh” on Rotten Tomatoes compared to “Supergirl’s” 52% “rotten” rating. So far, last summer’s “Superman,” which Gunn wrote and directed, is the most successful example of their quippy, poppy approach. It earned $618.7 million globally and was widely embraced by critics. The company’s streaming shows, which include “Lanterns” and “Peacemaker,” have been better received. articles.title: Box Office: A24’s ‘You Can See Everything’ Scores Huge $19.5 Million Second Weekend
articles.summary: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's twisty look at Elizabeth Holmes saw its grosses increase from its red-hot debut.
articles.content: Audiences continued to flock to “ You Can See Everything ,” as the twisty documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes captured the zeitgeist and saw its grosses increase in its second weekend. The A24 film earned $19.5 million over its sophomore frame, a 25% improvement from its $15.6 million opening. Few movies see their grosses rise like that. However, the film expanded its theater count, which helped lift ticket sales. “You Can See Everything” is playing in 2,655 theaters, up from the 855 it debuted on the previous weekend. Its popularity is remarkable considering that “You Can See Everything” is a three-hour documentary that is playing like a broadly commercial feature. It helped that A24 cloaked the film in secrecy , convincing audiences that the only way to avoid spoilers was to buy a ticket. Related Stories Watch ‘My Undesirable Friends’ Director Julia Loktev Recall the Week Russia Invaded Ukraine ‘Wildwood’ Sparked a Much-Needed Comeback for Laika at the Box Office Produced for a mere $7 million, “You Can See Everything” has grossed $45.1 million, positioning it to be one of the most successful non-fiction films in history. Michael Moore’s “Fahrenheit 9/11,” an anti-Bush treatise released in the midst of the contentious 2004 presidential election, remains the highest-grossing documentary with just over $222 million in receipts. “You Can See Everything” has easily topped “Melania,” which had been the year’s highest-grossing doc with its $16.3 million gross. That look at the gilded life of America’s First Lady was a lot less profitable given that Jeff Bezos and Amazon MGM Studios shelled out $40 million for the rights (they love non-fiction filmmaking!).
